17 A motor is used to lift a load vertically upwards.
The load has weight W.
The motor produces useful power output P.
The load is lifted at constant velocity v.
Which expression gives the time taken for the motor to lift the load vertically upwards through a
distance d ?
A
P
B
Wd
P
Wv
C
P
Wd
D
W
Pv

hints: Notice the useful work done lifting weight $W$ through distance $d$ is force times distance, so $W \times d$.
Recall useful power $P$ is the rate of doing that work, $P = \text{work}/t$.
Rearrange $P = Wd/t$ for $t$ and check that $Wd/P$ has units of joules over watts, which is seconds.
walkthrough: Identify the useful work: lifting force equals weight $W$ at constant velocity $v$, so for distance $d$ the work is $\text{work} = Wd$.
State the power rule: useful power output is work per unit time, $P = \text{work}/t$.
Rearrange for time by multiplying by $t$ and dividing by $P$: $t = Wd/P$.
Check units: $Wd$ is in $\text{J}$ and $P$ is in $\text{W} = \text{J s}^{-1}$, so $\text{J}/(\text{J s}^{-1}) = \text{s}$, correct for time. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is $P$ divided by $Wd$, which is $1/t$ not $t$, so it has units of $\text{s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: At constant velocity $Wv$ equals the useful power $P$, so $Wv/P$ is dimensionless and cannot be a time.

C.explanation: Useful work is $Wd$ and $P = \text{work}/t$, so $t = Wd/P$ with unit $\text{s}$.

D.explanation: $Pv/W$ mixes $P$ with $v$ incorrectly and does not equal work divided by power.
